headline: The internet is a network of networks—millions of connected computers sharing data through agreed protocols
universal_truth: Shared standards enable cooperation; agreement on rules creates capabilities beyond any individual
fun_facts: There are over 5 billion internet users—more than half of humanity
Data packets can take different routes to the same destination, reassembling at the end
The internet was designed to survive nuclear attack—no single point of failure can bring it down
discussion_questions: How has the internet changed how you live?
What would be impossible without the internet?
What problems has the internet created along with its benefits?

hook.script: Right now, you're connected to billions of computers worldwide. A message from Tokyo reaches New York in milliseconds. The internet is humanity's nervous system—a network of networks that transformed what's possible.

cliff.script: Billions of different devices, made by different companies, in different countries, somehow communicate seamlessly. How does this impossibly complex system actually work?
cliff.prompt: How do billions of different devices communicate?

options.text: They all agree on shared protocols—standard rules for formatting and transmitting data
options.response: Yes. Protocols like TCP/IP are the shared language. Agreement on standards lets anyone's device talk to anyone else's.

options.text: Large companies control the infrastructure and make everything compatible
options.response: Companies provide infrastructure, but the magic is in open protocols that anyone can implement...

fact1.title: Packet Paths
fact1.script: Data crosses the internet in packets—small chunks that may take different routes to the same destination. If one path fails, packets find another. This redundancy was built in—the internet was designed to survive even nuclear war.

fact2.title: Protocol Power
fact2.script: TCP/IP—Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol—is the internet's universal language. Every device that uses these protocols can communicate with every other. Shared standards turn chaos into coordination.

fact3.title: No Center
fact3.script: The internet has no center, no headquarters, no single controlling authority. It's a network of networks, each part independently operated but following common rules. Decentralization makes it resilient and global.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Shared standards enable cooperation. The internet teaches that agreement on rules creates capabilities beyond any individual. When billions cooperate through shared protocols, the impossible becomes routine.

outro.script: That's Day 120—four full months of learning together! We've explored body, nature, mind, and skills. Tomorrow, a new month begins. Until then, appreciate the network that connected us today.

growTrack.title: Internet Appreciation - See the Network
growTrack.learning_objective: Appreciate the infrastructure enabling digital life
growTrack.activity: When you use the internet today, pause to consider: your data is traveling through cables, routers, and servers across the world, following agreed protocols. Billions of dollars of infrastructure, decades of development, standards agreed by committees. All to load a webpage in seconds.
